target_name: Net Cash Cheapness With Accrual-Free Coverage
rationale: This is a one-input substitution (oancf → ib+dp) in an archived signal with identical economics and identical structure — a cosmetic coverage-driven variant rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the accrual-vs-cash distinction it discards is precisely the earnings-quality content the archive's other signals treat as informative.

target_name: Net Cash Cheapness With Dual Quality Screen
rationale: Internally consistent and thoughtfully constructed (SUMRANK avoids double multiplicative shrinkage), but it is an incremental blend of two already-tested legs whose quality inputs are likely correlated, so the additivity test is worth running yet unlikely to be a large step forward.

target_name: Net Liquid Claim Cheapness With Gross Profit
rationale: The valuation leg is essentially Graham's net-current-asset-value, a long-documented anomaly, but gating it on averaged gross profitability and contrasting it directly against the archived net-cash version is a legitimate and well-specified discrimination test rather than a plain rediscovery.

target_name: Enterprise Price Per Dollar Of Gross Profit
rationale: This is a direct rediscovery of the published enterprise-multiple anomaly (Loughran–Wellman), and the negative-EV rationale is shaky because the signal is non-monotone in cheapness — near-zero-EV firms rank mid-sample while the extreme long tail is populated by the sparse negative-EV cases the construct is being justified by.

target_name: Cheapness Backed By Working Liquid Assets
rationale: A coherent and genuinely diagnostic contrast to the archived B/M × current-asset-level signal, though revt/act is close to standard asset-turnover quality (an F-score ingredient) and is mechanically negatively related to act/at, so a result could partly just invert the earlier finding rather than explain it.

target_name: Rich Price On A Strained Balance Sheet
rationale: The sign diagnosis of prior short-side failures is the most intelligent reasoning in this batch and the expression's direction matches the stated hypothesis, but the glamour-plus-leverage combination is close to the documented distress/leverage-with-growth effect, and multiplying two [0,1] ranks leaves the long (low-value) leg an uninterpretable mix of cheap-and-strained with expensive-and-unstrained firms.
